rows.name: AccessGrant
rows.previousInvariantReview: One stable grant identity has one immutable set of scope/principal/effective terms and, once revoked, can never be reissued.

rows.name: Member
rows.previousInvariantReview: One tenant-user membership has one affiliation/expiry episode; deprovision closes authority and a fresh episode cannot start until authority cleanup completes.

rows.name: RolePermission
rows.previousInvariantReview: One normalized role-permission tuple has a single active relationship at a time.

rows.name: TeamMember
rows.previousInvariantReview: One tenant/team/member relationship is active only for one current membership episode.

rows.name: TeamRole
rows.previousInvariantReview: One tenant/team/role relationship has a single active assignment.

rows.name: PlatformOperatorRoster
rows.previousInvariantReview: There must always be at least one active platform operator, and only current operators can grant/revoke.

rows.name: UserIdentity
rows.previousInvariantReview: External provider+subject associates to exactly one platform user; revoked identity cannot authenticate and has one exact replacement.

00_AccessGrant.instructions: Considering the current source code for AccessGrant and the prior invariant review, is its aggregate boundary itself materially wrong or unproven? Focus on whether it combines independently changing lifecycles or splits an invariant that must be atomic; distinguish these boundary problems from command/retry/reactor implementation gaps that can be repaired without changing this aggregate boundary.

criteria.yes: Current code gives concrete evidence of a wrongly placed owner or a necessary aggregate-boundary proof missing.
criteria.no: The current owner is appropriate for its atomic invariant; remaining defects are command, identity, authorization, or reactor recovery implementation gaps.
